Pharmacometrics turns pharmacological questions into quantitative models that inform dose selection, study design and drug-development decisions. My work applies a consistent, reproducible workflow across non-compartmental, population and mechanistic methods, always anchored to the underlying pharmacology and to model diagnostics.

## The workflow

```{=html}
<div class="workflow">
  <span class="wf-step">Scientific question</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Data &amp; curation</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">EDA</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Model development</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Diagnostics</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Covariates / sensitivity</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Simulation</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Interpretation</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Reproducible report</span>
</div>
```

Each stage feeds the next: a clear question dictates the data specification; exploratory analysis shapes the structural model; diagnostics decide whether the model is trustworthy; covariate and sensitivity analyses probe robustness; and simulation translates the model back into clinically or scientifically meaningful predictions, all captured in a report that regenerates from code.

## Areas of focus

### Non-compartmental analysis (NCA)

Model-independent exposure metrics as the quantitative baseline: concentration–time profiling, C~max~/T~max~, AUC, half-life, clearance and volume, dose normalization and clinical PK interpretation. My professional day-to-day NCA work uses **Phoenix WinNonlin**; the portfolio projects use **PKNCA** in R.

### Population PK

Nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) modelling: structural model development, inter-individual and residual variability, covariate analysis, model diagnostics and simulation, building models that describe both the typical patient and the spread around them.

### PK/PD & exposure–response

Linking exposure to effect: direct and indirect (turnover) response models, E~max~ relationships, hysteresis, parameter estimation, simulation and sensitivity analysis, the basis for dose–response and dose-decision support.

### PBPK / mechanistic modelling

Physiologically based models with explicit tissue compartments and mechanistic disposition (metabolic and renal clearance), physiological parameterization, exposure prediction and scenario simulation, validated against observed data. *A developing focus area, demonstrated in the [caffeine PBPK](projects/caffeine-pbpk.qmd) project.*

### Model-based meta-analysis (MBMA)

Synthesising evidence across studies from published aggregate data: literature extraction, harmonization, aggregate-data modelling and interpretation of between-study variability, shown in the [acetaminophen MBMA](projects/acetaminophen-mbma.qmd) project.

## Diagnostics I rely on

::: {.panel}
Goodness-of-fit (DV vs PRED/IPRED, CWRES), visual predictive checks (VPC), η/ε-shrinkage, bootstrap-based parameter uncertainty, and forest plots for covariate effects and reproduction verdicts. A model is only as good as the diagnostics that scrutinise it.
:::
